notes:
A copyright notice is not a brand name, and an index page is not a thin article.

nhs.uk was told its brand appears two different ways — "title: NHS; Organization
schema: Crown Copyright". There is no publisher Organization on that site. The
only one anywhere sits inside the page node as
"copyrightHolder": {"@type": "Organization", "name": "Crown Copyright"}, the
legal rights regime covering UK government content, and the advice was to write
"NHS" into it verbatim.

Brand consistency now ignores names reached through copyrightHolder. The shared
schema helper still treats a copyright holder as the site's owner, because for
"which entity is this site" that is usually right; it is never the answer to
"what name is this site known by".

Thin-content advice also stopped assuming the reader is selling something, and
now carries the same index-page exception its very-thin sibling already had. An
A-Z of health conditions was being told to add pricing signals and a service
area, on the branch whose caveat had been written about that exact page.

Also corrects five pieces of prose that claimed the licence gate is inert in
shipped builds. It is not: shipped builds enforce, dev checkouts do not.
